readability.summary: The panel layout is documented where it is defined and at each place it passes through. The domain module says what a client's layout is, that it is presentation only and never a target, and what each field of a panel means for a hidden panel; the migration registry says why a step that changes no table exists; the protocol says which version has the layout messages and that a window names no client; the host's documentation says under which client it keeps the layout and what it does when its store fails; the window's backend says how the host's answers are matched to its requests. The new TypeScript module opens with what the window remembers, where each part of it is kept and why a change the host has not taken outranks the host's copy at the next start; its comments give the reason of the order in which a panel is given its size and its visibility. Tests name the behaviour they prove. Review against the final code named the first-layout contribution for what it is, since its old name had become the name of the layout record; replaced a roundabout check of a view's name by a function that says what it checks; dropped a second resize that changed nothing; made a constant relation a compile-time assertion; and made the module's note on Theia's own stored layout say what was observed of it. Examining why the first seeded defects did not fail the checks expected of them found that a hidden sidebar took its view from the last sample instead of the tab Theia notes for it, which the module now reads, and three weaknesses of the end-to-end test, which were mended: a check of an unreachable host that did not reach that path, a step that stopped the run on a seeded defect instead of failing a check, and a probe of the early paint that could ask a document the window never shows. The recheck before the commit read the code and the evidence record again, claim by claim against the logs, and mended three statements of the record that the logs did not bear out exactly (TASK-012_EVIDENCE.md sections 9 and 11).

The checkpoint note docs/evidence/TASK-012/CHECKPOINT.md, which the two checkpoint commits carried while the task was open, was removed when the evidence record replaced it. At the close, scripts/test/task_cleanup.py ran on the checkout with an empty TASK-012 manifest, first as a plan and then with --apply and its record: it removed nothing, refused nothing, and left in place 1 untracked files, the new source file and the TASK-012 evidence, each with its hash. The ignored files are the owner's IDE output (rust-analyzer's target/ and the Java extension's .gradle/ beside TASK-003's prototype) and the editor's link apps/desktop/node_modules, none task-owned, all left exactly as they are. The disposable installation and the scratch files of this task are removed once this receipt is committed and pushed; the Desktop build folder stays beside the Cargo target folder as a build cache, and the copy of the evidence scripts in /mnt/F/Nexees-toolchains/task-tools/ stays for the rest of this run of tasks. The machine was restarted during the first pause, which emptied the session scratch folder; the evidence scripts were restored from that copy. No pre-existing or user-owned file was deleted, reset or stashed, and no command of the task wrote in the owner's toolchain and cache folders: every tool of the task refuses to run without the isolated toolchain.
